title: Raspberry Pi 4 case
brief: A two-piece case for a Raspberry Pi 4 with a 30 mm fan on the lid. Leave the USB and Ethernet end open, raise the board on its mounting holes, and add vent slots under the CPU.
parts:
Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
30x30x10 mm 5V fan
4x M2.5 x 6 screws
techniques: shell() a rounded box to get walls and an open top
standoffs = cylinder minus pilot hole, fused per mounting hole
locating lip = rounded-rectangle ring extruded under the lid
PCB modelled as a printable:false reference body

components.name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
components.dims: PCB 85 × 56 × 1.4 mm; holes Ø2.7 on 58 × 49 mm, 3.5 mm from edge

print_notes: Base upright, lid upside down; no supports.
0.2 mm layers, 3 walls, 20% gyroid.

title: Arduino control box
brief: A desk control box for an Arduino Uno with a 1602 LCD in the lid and a rotary encoder knob. USB and power must stay reachable; add ventilation.
parts:
Arduino Uno R3
LCD1602 module
EC11 rotary encoder
techniques: port openings cut with makeBox at measured connector positions
display hung from lid standoffs so the glass sits in a window
panel-mount hole + anti-rotation slot for an encoder
fillet the outer rim inside try/catch

components.name: EC11 rotary encoder
components.dims: body 12 × 12 × 6.5; M7 bushing; Ø6 shaft; tab 7.8 mm from axis

print_notes: Box upright, lid upside down, no supports.
0.2 mm layers, 3 walls, 15% gyroid.

title: Snap-fit box
brief: A small 60 × 40 × 30 mm box with a lid that clicks on with snap hooks, no screws.
techniques: cantilever snap beam 1.6 mm thick with a barb that drops into a wall window
gap the locating lip where the beams are so they can flex
every sliding fit uses p.clearance
print_notes: Box upright; lid upside down so the beams print vertically (strong along the layers).
PETG or PLA+, 0.2 mm layers.

title: Desktop tape dispenser
brief: A weighted desktop tape dispenser for Scotch 3/4 inch tape on a 1 inch core, with a guide roller and a replaceable serrated blade under a clamp plate.
parts:
Scotch Magic Tape 3/4 in, 1 in core
Serrated dispenser blade 25 x 8 mm
M3 x 28 pin
techniques: drop-in U-slot seats an axle stub so the roll lifts out
hub drum = core ID minus 0.2 mm, axle stubs ride in the cheeks
roller on a metal pin, clamp plate screwed over a blade seat
washer pockets underneath add weight

components.name: Scotch Magic Tape 3/4 in
components.dims: 19.05 mm wide, 25.4 mm core, ~53 mm OD

print_notes: Body flat on its base; hub and roller standing on end.
Drop M20 washers into the base pockets for weight.

title: Print-in-place hinge
brief: A 40 mm print-in-place hinge with two screw-mount leaves that prints already assembled.
techniques: alternate knuckles between two leaves along one axis
the pin belongs to one leaf; the other leaf's knuckles get holes of pin + clearance
cut clearance cylinders out of each leaf where the other leaf's knuckles turn
use clearance ≥ 0.35 mm for print-in-place
print_notes: Print flat as modelled; no supports.
First layer must be clean so the knuckles don't fuse; flex it gently to free it.

title: Spur gear pair
brief: A 2:1 spur gear pair, module 2, on a base plate with pegs so it can be turned by hand.
techniques: involute tooth profile generated point by point and drawn with lineTo
centre distance = m(z1+z2)/2 + backlash
rotate one gear half a pitch so teeth mesh
bores = shaft + clearance; pegs on a base plate
print_notes: Gears flat; 0.12–0.16 mm layers for clean teeth.
Base flat; no supports.

title: 5-slot cable organizer
techniques: keyhole slot = seat cylinder + narrower throat box
V lead-in drawn as a polygon on XZ and extruded through
label grooves and washer pockets as simple cuts

components.name: Phone charging cable
components.dims: jacket Ø3.0–4.5 mm; connector head ≥ 8 × 6 mm

print_notes: Upright on its base, no supports.
Pause at ~4 mm to drop in steel washers.

title: Phone stand
brief: A desk phone stand that holds a phone in a case at a comfortable reading angle, with a slot for the charging cable.
techniques: rotate() boxes to build angled rests and struts
cut a big box below z=0 to flatten the bottom after rotating
reference phone placed resting on the surfaces to prove fit

components.name: Phone in a case
components.dims: up to 9–11 mm thick, 72–80 mm wide

print_notes: Print on its side for strength along the rest, or upright with no supports.

title: Under-desk headphone hook
brief: A headphone hook that screws to the underside of a desk.
techniques: draw a J-profile on XZ and extrude it across the width
countersink = through hole + loft from the head diameter to the shank
fillet edges along the extrude direction with inDirection("Y")
print_notes: Print on its side (profile flat) so the layers run around the J.

title: Bud vase
brief: A 120 mm bud vase with a smooth curved profile and decorative rings.
techniques: profile with smoothSplineTo, revolved around Z
shell() to hollow, with a revolved inner profile as fallback
rings cut as thin annular cylinders
print_notes: Upright; works in vase mode if you drop the rings.
Line with a glass tube for water.

title: Desk owl
brief: A small desk owl figurine about 65 mm tall: round body, big eyes, ear tufts, folded wings, sitting on a turned round base. Prints in one piece without supports.
techniques: overlapping ellipsoids fuse into smooth organic forms
rotate small ellipsoids for tufts and wings
lofted beak tapering to a point
flat cut bottom + revolved base
print_notes: Upright on the base, no supports.
0.12–0.16 mm layers for the curves.

title: Desk robot
brief: A friendly little robot figurine for a desk, about 70 mm tall, printable in one piece.
techniques: rounded boxes = makeBaseBox + fillet(all edges) in try/catch
spheres at joints hide where cylinders meet
eye sockets cut, pupils fused back in
flat feet for bed adhesion
print_notes: Upright; arms stay under 45°.
0.12 mm layers for the details.
